subject: Deal-driven GPU pool allocation for NovaHealth: US/EU/APAC sizing request
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sizing ask: NovaHealth + CloudOps APAC demand

Team —

We have two linked commitments coming in that will materially change our dedicated pool footprint if we convert to reserved capacity: NovaHealth (enterprise contract, deal NH-2026-Q4-3221) and a CloudOps channel onboarding that will push APAC traffic. High level numbers from sales: expected steady-state token throughput ~6m tokens/day, peak concurrency ~600 active streams, regional traffic split roughly 60/25/15 (US/EU/APAC).

I attached a working sheet (Q4_gpu_plan_v2.xlsx) with a simple cost model; I need a recommended reserved capacity plan by region and a fallback arrangement for burst for APAC. Specifically:
- Reserved GPU count per region (suggested hardware family and perf assumptions)
- Expected headroom for burst and recommended partners/regions for immediate fill
- Lead times to provision dedicated pools and any procurement blockers
- Quick note on whether these deals should request financial commitment adjustments to align with capacity (e.g., 12-month ramp)

Can you please review and share a concise recommendation by EOD Thu Nov 26? I'll be coordinating with Emily at NovaHealth and want to include a Mutual Action Plan in the next touch.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

Attachment: Q4_gpu_plan_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sizing ask: NovaHealth + CloudOps APAC demand

Sean / all —

Quick read of the numbers and our current pool availability suggests the following conservative reserved plan (assumes models are running on quantized A100/RTX-class variants):

US: 48 x A100-80GB reserved (handles ~370 concurrent streams at 1.2s token latency, 60% traffic)
EU: 18 x A100-80GB reserved + 6 x smaller V100-like systems for regional low-latency bursts (handles ~150 concurrent, 25% traffic)
APAC: 8 x A100-80GB reserved (short lead) + 8 x burst capacity via CloudOps partner (ops@cloudopssolutions.com) to reach 16 total on demand (handles 15% traffic).

Notes and caveats:
- APAC tightness: our on-prem partner pools in APAC are scarce — lead time for dedicated racks in region is 6–8 weeks unless we leverage partner capacity as burst.
- If NovaHealth wants guaranteed APAC latency SLOs, we should either increase APAC reserved to 12 or commit to a hybrid reserved+partner SLA.
- Cost-opt: consider 4:1 reserved:burst ratio initially and revisit after two months of telemetry.

I attached a quick region map (capacity_map_us_eu_apac.png) and updated the numbers in the spreadsheet.

- Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Dedicated Sales Operations
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachment: capacity_map_us_eu_apac.png (image stub)
From: Emily Chen <emily@novahealth.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudOps Solutions <ops@cloudopssolutions.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 07:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sizing ask: NovaHealth + CloudOps APAC demand

Thanks, Sean + Marissa —

We appreciate the proposed plan. A couple of clarifications from our side before we sign the MAP:
- Confirmed traffic split is similar to what you have: ~60% US, 25% EU, 15% APAC. APAC is small today but expected to grow by 2x in Q1 with new partners in SEA.
- Lead time is the main blocker for us — we need a guarantee that APAC latency <= 250ms for user-facing flows. If reserved capacity in APAC can be increased to cover 75% of peak within 30 days, that meets our ramp needs.
- Are there options to prepay a smaller APAC commitment and have burst credit that automatically converts to reserved if utilization stays high?

We can sign if we have a clear MAP with timelines and an escape hatch on billing if growth doesn't materialize. Happy to hop on a short call to align this afternoon PST.

Best,
Emily Chen
Head of Platform, NovaHealth
emily@novahealth.ai
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 10:20:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Sizing ask: NovaHealth + CloudOps APAC demand

I ran the numbers with infra — a few concrete suggestions to present to NovaHealth: 

1) APAC rapid-fill plan: convert 8 on-demand equivalents to reserved within 30 days by staging capacity in our partner pool (CloudOps in SYD). Add a convertible credit line on the invoice that can be applied to reserved purchases within 90 days.

2) EU optimization: use mixed instance types (2 x A100 + 6 x 40GB T4-style agile nodes) for long-tail work to keep reserved count lower and reduce cost.

3) Lead-time mitigation: we can ship a 'soft reserve' (contracted capacity, not yet provisioned) to hold capacity for 60 days while we finalize procurement — this gives commercial confidence without immediate provisioning.

I'll prepare a one-page MAP and a short SLA clause for APAC latency (subject to partner certs). Linking the proposed DocuSign template: https://docusign.com/link/abc123

- Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Infra Partnerships
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

1) Can Rohan confirm if we can reserve 8x A100-equivalent in APAC partner pool (SYD) and the steps/timeline to convert to dedicated in-region if NovaHealth converts credits?
2) Lauren — commercial: please draft a MAP that includes a 30-day convertible credit for APAC and an SLA clause for regional latency (<=250ms) subject to partner certs.
3) Marissa/Rishi — please produce a 1-page cost appendix (commitment vs burst) to include in the contract.

Customer is ready to sign once we have the above and the DocuSign is updated. Attaching the summary we're sending to the customer: commitment_summary_NH.pdf

Thanks — please mark urgent and reply with timelines.

Sean
